title: Which data migration tool fits you?

questions.hint: The post says migration is really four different jobs, so start here.

options.label: Business apps and databases for reports
options.why: you want a warehouse fed from apps and databases

options.label: Inside AWS
options.why: the Azure DMS overview names Azure SQL targets and the Google DMS overview names Google Cloud databases

options.label: A cloud database on Azure or Google Cloud
options.why: the Azure DMS overview names Azure SQL targets and the Google DMS overview names Google Cloud databases

options.label: BigQuery
options.why: the Google DMS overview lists Google Cloud databases and no warehouse, and the Azure DMS overview names Azure SQL targets

options.label: An Iceberg or Parquet lake I run
options.why: the Azure DMS overview names Azure SQL targets and the Google DMS overview names Google Cloud databases

options.label: A warehouse or lake somewhere else
options.why: the Azure DMS overview names Azure SQL targets and the Google DMS overview names Google Cloud databases

options.label: One move, then switch over
options.why: the cloud migration services handle one-time moves

options.label: Keep copying changes, minutes are fine
options.why: you want ongoing syncs and can live with some delay

options.label: Live, in both directions
options.why: GoldenGate documents one-way and two-way setups

questions.q: What does your budget look like?

options.label: Free or close to it
options.why: some have a free route: Airbyte Core, Fivetran's free plan, GoldenGate Free for Oracle databases up to 20 GB, Google's no-charge native moves and OLake Go's open-source licence (you still pay for servers)

options.label: A price I can work out from the vendor page
options.why: DataSync is a flat per-GB fee and AWS DMS lists an hourly rate

options.label: A paid enterprise licence is fine
options.why: GoldenGate is sold by licence, listed per processor or Named User Plus

options.label: A cloud or vendor service
options.why: you want the provider to run it

options.label: My own team, on our own servers
options.why: Airbyte Core is self-managed and you run OLake Go on your own infrastructure

awsdms.name: AWS Database Migration Service
awsdms.summary: One-time moves or ongoing replication between databases, billed by instance hours or Serverless DCU hours.
awsdms.bestWhen: you are moving a database into AWS.
awsdms.watchOut: AWS says there is no SLA for CDC latency, and its target list names S3, Kinesis, Kafka and others but not Iceberg (the guide's AWS DMS section links the page).

azuredms.name: Azure Database Migration Service
azuredms.summary: Moves SQL Server databases to Azure SQL targets; the only pricing page we found is for the classic service.
azuredms.bestWhen: you are moving SQL Server into Azure SQL.
azuredms.watchOut: Microsoft's notice says the classic version for SQL Server scenarios was not supported after 15 March 2026, the overview table does not list assessment or login migration for the portal version, and it names Azure SQL targets only, so confirm other sources and targets with Microsoft.

googledms.name: Google Database Migration Service
googledms.summary: One-time or continuous moves into Google Cloud databases, with no additional charge for native same-engine moves to Cloud SQL or AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.
googledms.bestWhen: the target is Cloud SQL or AlloyDB.
googledms.watchOut: destinations are Google Cloud databases only, and no lake or warehouse is listed.

goldengate.name: Oracle GoldenGate
goldengate.summary: Copies between many systems, including one-way and two-way setups; Oracle's FAQ says it delivers changes in real time.
goldengate.bestWhen: your estate is Oracle-heavy, or a copy has to run both ways.
goldengate.watchOut: Oracle's price list charges per processor or Named User Plus, and Iceberg writing sits in a separate product.

datasync.name: AWS DataSync
datasync.summary: Online transfer of files and objects into AWS storage, with checks that the copy matches.
datasync.bestWhen: file shares, archives or object stores are heading into AWS.
datasync.watchOut: the pages we read name file and object storage only, and S3 and other AWS charges come on top.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: Managed pipelines from databases, apps and files into warehouses and lakes, billed on Monthly Active Rows.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to run the pipelines into a warehouse.
fivetran.watchOut: the decision table rules it out for a one-time database cutover, and its Iceberg service does not support position deletes.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: Syncs from many sources into warehouses, databases and lakes, with a free self-run Core edition.
airbyte.bestWhen: you want many connectors and are fine with scheduled syncs.
airbyte.watchOut: CDC runs on a schedule and Cloud Standard syncs at most hourly, so the decision table rules it out for a one-time cutover.

datastream.name: Google Cloud Datastream
datastream.summary: A serverless service that backfills, then captures changes into BigQuery, Cloud Storage or Iceberg tables in BigQuery.
datastream.bestWhen: you are on Google Cloud and landing data in BigQuery.
datastream.watchOut: a processed byte can be 2 to 5 times the real data size, its Iceberg mode is append-only, and Google documents no self-hosted option.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source copies of databases, S3 files and Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg or Parquet on storage you run, with change capture for PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server.
olake.bestWhen: you want an Iceberg or Parquet lake and want to run the tool on your own infrastructure.
olake.watchOut: output is Apache Iceberg or Parquet, and Oracle, Db2 and S3 sources load by full refresh or incremental copy.
